final_answer:
A deadlock in concurrent programming occurs when multiple processes are waiting for each other to release resources they need. Four necessary conditions must be met for a deadlock to occur: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, and circular wait. 

To prevent mutual exclusion, shared resources can be allowed. Hold and wait can be prevented by requiring processes to release all resources before requesting new ones. No preemption can be addressed by allowing resource preemption. Circular wait can be broken by imposing a total ordering on resource requests. Each condition must be addressed to prevent deadlocks in concurrent programming.
